- **[HARD] FIRST-CLASS MACHINE-CHECKED SEAM (sound re-import) ✕ Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *FIRST-CLASS MACHINE-CHECKED SEAM (sound re-import), Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT, Zero-cost — all proofs, INCLUDING seam obligations, erase at compile time*
  - surfaced by: The SEAM construct — give the formal syntax and typing of the seam: how ordinary (safe) code enters proof-land, what machine-checked obligation it discharges there, and how it re-exports a CHECKED SAFE INTERFACE that ordinary code then uses WITHOUT itself crossing the seam. Give formation / introduction / elimination rules.
  - A decidable, erasable obligation logic cannot soundly gate the foundational primitives' heap-level preconditions — The seam must concentrate on allocators, atomics, lock-free structures, and MMIO, whose real safety conditions are aliasing/provenance/temporal heap facts (interior-&mut non-aliasing, post-load index freshness, initialization, never-freed reachability, address stability). A decidable, proof-free theory over NLL-nameable places cannot state these; stretching it to (e.g.) a[i+1] over symbolic bounds reduces from halting, so it cannot stay decidable. Keeping it decidable forces the obligation to drop or weaken the precondition, laundering UB into safe code (Seam-Elim with no pre_j, TOCTOU over atomics). Zero-cost erasure removes the only escape — a runtime witness — because an erased static token cannot bind mutable/temporal state, and the one fix (freeze state via a shared borrow) destroys the &mut that indexed-mutation exports need, pushing ordinary code back across the seam.
- **[HARD] Sound re-import ✕ Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Sound re-import, Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT, Zero-cost — all proofs, INCLUDING seam obligations, erase at compile time*
  - surfaced by: The SAFE FRAGMENT — ADOPT Rust's Non-Lexical-Lifetimes borrow checker as shipped (hardcoded, decidable, proof-free) for ordinary single-threaded code. Do NOT re-derive it. State only the SAFE INTERFACE it presents to the seam: what a seam-crossed primitive must hand back for safe code to use it without proofs.
  - Sound re-import needs a linearity witness NLL's region-only vocabulary cannot carry — Every seam primitive that matters mints a unique mutable capability from a shared, Copy handle (alloc(&self)->&mut, borrow_mut(&self), split, view->uniq), so its soundness is a value-level uniqueness/linearity fact. Zero-cost-plus-concentration forces that fact to be discharged once at definition and erased, but NLL — the adopted proof-free safe fragment — checks only duplicable lexical regions and has no linear or interior-mutability modality, so the witness cannot be re-expressed in the type system that must consume it. The fact must therefore give one of three ways, each fatal: dropped (a second call on the Copy handle re-mints two live aliasing &mut that NLL accepts), kept faithfully (heap-reachability separation-logic entailment, undecidable — RustBelt/Lithium), or re-checked per use (ordinary code crosses the seam everywhere — the ATS2 cliff). The duplicated-handle / two-calls-on-one-capability pattern exposes it identically in all four revisions.
- **[HARD] FIRST-CLASS MACHINE-CHECKED SEAM (machine-checked, sound, one toolchain / no external prover) ✕ Sound re-import (no unsound obligation launders UB into safe code)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *FIRST-CLASS MACHINE-CHECKED SEAM (machine-checked, sound, one toolchain / no external prover), Sound re-import (no unsound obligation launders UB into safe code), Seam CONCENTRATION of the foundational concurrent/low-level primitives (atomics, lock-free, MMIO) behind it*
  - surfaced by: BEHIND THE SEAM — concretely, what obligation does a foundation author discharge, in-language, to implement (a) a lock-free SPSC queue, (b) an MMIO read-to-clear register, (c) an intrusive doubly-linked list — and how does each re-export a safe interface the safe fragment can use without proofs?
  - A decidably machine-checked seam cannot soundly verify the concurrent primitives it must concentrate — Concentration forces exactly the hard primitives (atomics, lock-free SPSC, MMIO, relaxed memory, intrusive aliasing) onto the seam, and the only logic that soundly specifies them — concurrent separation logic with ghost state, a relaxed-memory model, and Send/Sync — has an undecidable, certificate-free discharge problem (a {True}call{φ_M} axiom set derives False iff M halts). So any obligation the one-toolchain kernel can actually decide is strictly weaker than the true signature denotation, and the missing conjunct is always thread-safety or the memory model: weaken the logic and it rejects the SPSC outright (Rev 0); keep it expressive and the consistency check goes undecidable (Rev 1); make it checkable and it omits Send/Sync, re-exporting an na_inv type as Sync into a data race (Rev 2), or omits the signature denotation, aliasing &mut in proof-free safe code and citing the SC theorem for a relaxed Π that shipped the iRC11 Arc race (Rev 3). Decidable-and-machine-checked or sound-re-import — one must give.
- **[HARD] first-class machine-checked seam (sound re-import) ✕ decidable and proof-free safe fragment via a hardcoded structural borrow checker**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *first-class machine-checked seam (sound re-import), decidable and proof-free safe fragment via a hardcoded structural borrow checker, executable specification — one toolchain, no external prover*
  - surfaced by: SEAM SOUNDNESS / re-import — the rule that makes crossing BACK sound: how does the safe fragment trust a seam-crossed primitive without re-verifying it, and what structurally stops an unsound obligation from laundering UB into safe code?
  - Sound re-import needs a semantic heap invariant the structural borrow checker cannot carry — Sound re-import is a whole-heap, representation-level property (no live value invalidated, no hidden alias, valid bit-pattern, refcount accounted), but the safe fragment's checker is by concession a syntactic, per-value, decidable borrow checker that maintains no such predicate. So any obligation cheap enough for the checker to consume and erase governs only the named exit slot and leaves the frame open — exactly the pattern that recurred every revision: a bump allocator returns overlapping &mut, a raw store corrupts a sibling's live MaybeUninit payload, a no-op self-CAS re-mints a confined capability, a persistent Arc duplicates without a refcount bump. Making the obligation strong enough to close the frame converts 'Inv' from a finite adoptable table into RustBelt's semantic logical-relations model and its fundamental theorem — which is not decidable, not proof-free, does not erase as a finite witness, and is the external prover the single-toolchain spec forbids. The bridge between structural ownership facts and the semantic value relation is the incompatibility, not any one seam construct.
- **[HARD] sound re-import (crossing back launders no UB into safe code) ✕ decidable AND proof-free safe fragment over a hardcoded Rust-style borrow checker**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *sound re-import (crossing back launders no UB into safe code), decidable AND proof-free safe fragment over a hardcoded Rust-style borrow checker, zero-cost erasure with seam concentration*
  - surfaced by: SEAM CONCENTRATION & ergonomics — the language mechanism and the argument that keep ordinary code from ever crossing the seam (the checked-interface boundary), and why the obligation stays with a handful of foundation authors. Exhibit a realistic program where ~99% of code is seam-free.
  - Sound re-import needs invariants the fixed proof-free checker provably cannot encode — A zero-cost seam can only hand its guarantee back as a witness in the safe fragment's fixed NLL+affinity vocabulary, but the foundations concentration depends on prove invariants strictly stronger than that vocabulary can express — happens-before from relaxed atomics, relational i≠j, cardinality ≤N, must-run liveness, variance/Send/dropck. So re-import must either drop the un-encodable conjunct, yielding UB in pure safe code (split2(0,0) gives two &mut to one cell; a relaxed-linearizable object lets weak-memory-blind code reason sequentially and accept a data race), or keep the obligation alive in ordinary code, reinstating the per-call ATS2 proof tax concentration was meant to abolish. Concentration cannot rescue it because the foundation proofs are themselves Iris-grade and open (per-structure custom cameras / synchronized ghost state), hence neither decidable nor closeable into a handful of AI-legible reusable primitives.
- **[HARD] Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT ✕ Sound re-import**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT, Sound re-import, Seam CONCENTRATION*
  - surfaced by: ZERO-COST SEAM ERASURE — how every seam obligation/witness erases at compile time with a formal guarantee it leaves no runtime trace.
  - A decidable proof-free seam logic is too weak to soundly re-import foundational primitives — Zero-cost erasure deletes any runtime trap/check identically to an honest proof, so each crossing's soundness must be discharged statically; to keep ordinary code decidable and proof-free, that static logic collapses to UTVPI/QF-LIA-bounded refinements. But the real invariants of the named primitives are not in any such fragment — allocator size is nonlinear (rows*cols*sizeof≤CAP), split_at_mut is disjointness/ownership (RustBelt's Iris, not arithmetic), and ℤ-indices versus modular usize make the weak logic actively unsound (reflect injects m=2⁶⁴; one-sided NoWrap underflows hi−lo to −2 → erased OOB). Strengthening the logic to discharge them soundly makes it undecidable and proof-bearing and pushes SMT/proofs into ordinary callers, collapsing concentration; so one of decidable-proof-free, sound-re-import, or concentration must give.
